subject: Aligning forecast categories & quick training — Action required
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: sales-ops@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning forecast categories & quick training — Action required

Team,

Quick update and an ask: finance and sales ops finalized small but important changes to how we label forecast categories. We need everyone to update open opportunities and attend a short training so the next commit run is clean.

Summary of changes (effective immediately):
- Commit: Signed PO or written executive signoff + legal procurement loop complete. Default probability: 90%.
- Best Case: Strong customer intent with expected close this quarter but missing either executive signoff or legal PO. Default probability: 60%.
- Pipeline: All open opportunities that are not in Best Case/Commit. Default probability: 30%.

Why this matters: our new finance cadence will treat Commit as the only category counted toward the committed forecast for bookings and ARR recognition planning. Best Case remains for close monitoring but not included in committed numbers.

Action items (please do both within 48 hours):
1) Update stage/category on all open opportunities in the CRM per the attached definitions (attached: forecast-definitions-v2.pdf).
2) RSVP to the 30-minute training on Thu, Mar 12 at 10:00 PT (calendar invite attached: training-invite.ics). I will go over decision rules and a handful of examples from your pipelines.

If you have a deal you think should move to Commit but doesn’t meet the criteria, include the deal id and a one-line rationale in reply and we’ll review on the call.

Thanks — we need a clean commit line for the CFO run next week.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: forecast-definitions-v2.pdf, training-invite.ics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning forecast categories & quick training — Action required

Laura —

Thanks for the clarity. Quick question: when you say "legal procurement loop complete," do we need a countersigned PO or is an explicit, dated email from procurement confirming billing terms sufficient? Also, do reseller-sourced POs (partners) count as Commit if the partner has provided a signed PO but the end customer hasn't signed with us yet?

CC'ing Karthik for the partner guidance.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, West
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning forecast categories & quick training — Action required

Marissa —

Good questions. Short answers:
- Countersigned PO preferred for Commit. If you have a dated procurement confirmation from the customer (an email from procurement/purchasing confirming the PO or intent to bill with explicit terms) plus no outstanding legal terms, that can be considered Commit — we’ll validate on the training call.
- Partner/reseller POs are treated case-by-case. If the partner provides a PO and the deal has clear legal/financial acceptance (and we have the partner agreement in place), we can consider Commit. If there’s ambiguity at the end-customer level, keep as Best Case until we have explicit confirmation.

I uploaded a short playbook excerpt with examples to the sales drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/forecast-playbook (see the "Commit vs Best Case examples" doc).

Training details: Thu, Mar 12 — 10:00–10:30 PT. I'll cover the decision rules and run 6 live examples. Please bring 1–2 deals you'd like reviewed (deal ids in subject). I created the calendar invite and will record.

If anyone has urgent deals to adjudicate before the call, reply with the deal id and one-line rationale and I’ll triage.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Related links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1234
From: Alicia Mendez <alicia@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning forecast categories & quick training — question about Acme deal
Hey Karthik / Marissa —

Quick question on our side — we sent the signed SOW last week to your legal team and our procurement team is aligned, but I haven't seen a countersigned PO back. From Acme's perspective we consider this committed. Will Redwood treat our deal as Commit without the countersigned PO?

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Mendez
Director of Data & AI, Acme Corp
alicia@acme.com

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the note and congrats on getting the SOW signed. For Redwood's commit definition we need either a countersigned PO or explicit procurement confirmation that includes billing terms and an acknowledged invoice schedule. Since you mention procurement is aligned, could you forward the procurement confirmation email (the one to your legal or finance team that references billing terms) to procurement@redwood.com and cc me? If procurement confirmation arrives before the CFO run, we will treat the deal as Commit. Otherwise, we'll leave it as Best Case and review during the training queue — not a blocker on support onboarding, just our internal forecast policy.

Example: for RDW-ACME-2026-01 we currently have the SOW and a sales-signed order form; I marked it Best Case pending the procurement confirmation. If you ping procurement@redwood.com with your confirmation, we can update immediately.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales Operations
